public_source_heads.source_scope: Windows raw-fd API/position semantics, release-level locking correctness, dependency floor selection

exact_continuation: Fresh-bootstrap first. Re-read root manifest and open_source config, then use RUN_20260828_1907_EVENT_AUTHORITY_API.md. First determine whether any current production path can continue writing <project_root>/.argus/events.jsonl after events.migration-v2.json exists; if yes, the existence-only marker can permanently miss later legacy rows and shared authority alone is insufficient, so specify source-signature/replay semantics or prove the writer unreachable. Then finalize the core/event_store.py API and cross-process tests, apply candidate013 regression mapping, and continue candidate009/011 byte-stable snapshot, strict events.lock -> mission-view.lock, PlannerVerdict FOUND/ABSENT/UNKNOWN, and explicit iter_call_events corruption behavior. Keep candidate008 durability and candidate005 provenance separate.

run_findings.candidate_014_writer_inventory: Targeted source classification found three production events.jsonl append mechanisms and no fourth: JsonlEventSink._append; AgentIOLogger.log->_jsonl_append; ensure_project_events_standardized. Search false positives were classified as readers or writes to transcript/inbox/backlog. AgentIO raw agent_io.jsonl remains a separate bounded debug artifact and must not use canonical event authority.
run_findings.candidate_014_agent_io_path_classes: AgentCliBackend._agent_io_log_path routes a configured project to <project_root>/events.jsonl; without project usage context it may use ARGUS_SKILL_AGENT_IO_LOG or <working_dir>/.argus/events.jsonl. Separate backend instances can write concurrently, so the instance-local AgentIO lock is not a same-file authority.
run_findings.candidate_014_core_api: Smallest import-safe boundary is a core event-store primitive: EventLogAuthorityError as an OSError subclass; event_log_authority(log_path) using os.open(...,0600), a real file object, Portalocker LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB, retry only AlreadyLocked, permanent failures surfaced as the domain OSError, and best-effort post-commit unlock/close; plus isolate_unterminated_tail_unlocked(log_path). Normalization, sink-configured rotation, and Mission View semantics stay outside this low-level layer.
run_findings.candidate_014_fail_soft_compat: AgentIOLogger._jsonl_append currently catches OSError only. Letting raw Portalocker LockException escape from the shared authority would newly allow logging failure to break provider execution. A domain OSError preserves the adapter's fail-soft contract while JsonlEventSink can still return False and migration can retry later.
run_findings.candidate_014_migration_scope: ensure_project_events_standardized computes legacy sources, scans canonical identities, appends and fsyncs canonical rows under events.migration-v2.lock but not events.lock; shared canonical authority must cover canonical identity scan + delimiter isolation + append. The next unresolved question is whether existence-only migration marker semantics are safe against any continuing legacy .argus/events.jsonl writer.
run_findings.candidate_013_regression_map: Patch/test placement is concrete: event_catalog.py adds ROUND_REVIEW_STARTED to SIGNAL_EVENT_TYPES; mission_view/_dispatch.py and _view_state.py remove ENGINEER_PROGRESS from durable projection; tests/test_event_verbosity.py covers default/signal reviewer-start persistence and ordinary-progress negative; tests/core/test_mission_view.py carries the durable-event/default-signal invariant and reviewer-active state coverage.
run_findings.candidate_012_dependency_floor: portalocker>=4.2 remains the first defensible floor for the inspected raw-fd Windows locking surface; current Argus still declares portalocker>=3.
run_findings.candidate_011_ordering_revised: All canonical writers must share pre-record delimiter isolation. Sink order: authority -> delimiter -> rotation -> new row -> Mission View projection. AgentIO/migration likewise isolate before their new rows. Never truncate damaged bytes; stable reading remains byte-row based.
run_findings.candidate_010_supervisor_contract: FOUND skips re-emit then acknowledges; ABSENT alone authorizes one re-emit after complete stable clean scan; UNKNOWN covers snapshot/open/decode/target-relevant parse ambiguity, leaves outbox pending, and returns PLAN_RETRY without Planner invocation.
run_findings.candidate_007_windows_bootstrap_race: Mission View reconciliation still needs strict events.lock -> mission-view.lock and a writer projection entry point that does not recursively reacquire event authority.
run_findings.candidate_008_status: unchanged separate power-loss durability hypothesis; no power-loss incident reproduced
run_findings.candidate_005_transition_lineage_patch: optional existing Manager intent ID -> stage_history transition_id remains provenance-only and separate
run_findings.control_freeze: semantic work froze on note SHA d6a6857ade76e9f6d89a0bb42e987d44f4571a90 control15/config6. Later note heads, including 35dfba52623ca0927500aed433a53b0961105fe6 and 21cf9e514866f243b3f5ad041fb0bf7690c7de1e, were observed only for authorized write coordination; newer control semantics were not adopted.
run_findings.connector_mutation_boundary: Only role-local checkpoint/LATEST and immutable open_source receipt writes are authorized. No branch/ref/source/control/other-worker/downstream/legacy/shared-ledger mutation was performed. The first checkpoint create attempt hit a 409 due concurrent note-head movement and made no write; the retry created the checkpoint successfully.
